findings.desc: CHK-002 userSees pins a literal tamper message that is itself the stale-enumeration defect this story removes, and the implementer correctly REFUSED to ship it. The pinned text names the signed fields as "(agentResults/issues/background/title/description/checklist were modified)" - a hand-written enumeration that goes wrong the next time the domain changes. What shipped instead renders the domain from its single declaration (INIT_CHECK_SIGNATURE_DOMAIN), which is what plan.md DoneWhen and the dispatch both asked for. AUTHOR OF THE DEFECT: the main agent, when writing the acceptance field in PLAN. The implementer flagged the conflict and reported it rather than silently self-correcting or silently complying, which is the correct behaviour. userSees is frozen from DEV (checklist_update refuses it by design, so the executor cannot move the acceptance goalposts) - this finding is the sanctioned channel for recording that the pinned criterion was superseded. RESOLUTION SOUGHT: accept the rendered message as satisfying CHK-002 acceptance, on the record, rather than reopening PLAN to edit the field. The shipped behaviour is strictly better than the pinned text.
findings.dismissReason: Accepting the shipped behaviour as satisfying CHK-002, on the record. The pinned userSees text was authored by me in PLAN and is itself the stale-enumeration defect this story removes; the implementer refused to ship it and reported the conflict rather than silently complying or silently self-correcting, which is the behaviour the freeze exists to produce. What shipped renders the field list from INIT_CHECK_SIGNATURE_DOMAIN, which is strictly better and is what plan.md DoneWhen asked for. Reopening PLAN to edit one acceptance sentence would cost a phase round-trip to make the record cosmetically consistent with a worse requirement. The docs lane independently verified the shipped message against source and found it correct.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: computeInitCheckVerdictHash (packages/main/src/core/init-check-gate.ts:169-178) defines a NEW private module-scoped canonicalJson(value) — recursive key-sorted, undefined-dropping JSON canonicalization — duplicating logic that already exists as the exported canonicalJson in packages/main/src/core/digest.ts:36-38, whose own header comment says it was extracted into a leaf module specifically "so it can be reused without dragging handler dependencies along" (already reused by core/review-run.ts). init-check-gate.ts already imports nothing else from digest.ts, so nothing blocks reuse; the two implementations sort keys by different comparators (digest.ts: a.localeCompare(b); init-check-gate.ts: a<b?-1:a>b?1:0) and diverge on null-vs-array handling, so this is not a byte-identical duplicate — it is a second, subtly different canonicalization routine for a signature/hashing code path, which is exactly the kind of unintentional near-duplicate that should not survive introducing a new signed-hash helper.
findings.resolvedReason: NOT de-duplicated, on measurement: the two canonicalizations DIVERGE, so swapping would have changed the digest of already-signed records. Compared them side by side over 24 payload shapes (canonical/fallback/no-agentResults records plus the malformed agentResults encodings the verdict hash must keep distinct: {}, 'garbage', 0, null, [], nested arrays, undefined holes, garbage issues, unicode/mixed-case/numeric-string/empty-string keys, deep nesting): 20 AGREE, 4 DIVERGE. (1) digest.ts sorts keys with a.localeCompare(b), which is default-locale-dependent - measured on this Node, LANG=sv_SE puts key 'a-umlaut' after 'z' while en-US/de-DE puts it after 'a', and it orders 'a' before 'B'; the private copy uses code-unit order and is identical on every host. A locale-dependent signature would report init_check_tampered on an untouched record verified on a differently configured machine. (2) digest.ts rebuilds a plain object, so JSON.stringify emits integer-like keys first in numeric order regardless of its sort ({"2","10"}) where the private copy emits its own lexicographic order ({"10","2"}). (3) producer-side only: digest.ts drops function/symbol members and stringifies bigint; the private copy keeps them as null and lets bigint throw. Both (1) and (2) are reachable from a hand-edited file, which is exactly the input class this hash exists to catch. The swap moves none of the 267 live init-check.json files (measured), but the domain claims totality over arbitrary on-disk content, so that is not the property being defended. Action taken instead: init-check-gate.ts:162-194 now carries the measured divergence and states that removing the copy is a deliberate migrated signature-algorithm change, never a cleanup. digest.ts is outside this story's allowedModify and was not touched. Verified: npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/main clean, build clean, red-b8df9-init-check-verdict-signature.mjs 0 RED / 24 rows, red-b8df9-chk002-verdict-shapes.mjs 0 FAILED / 17 rows. Commit e05bdb6112.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/init-preflight.ts:136-138 (initCheckRow) still open-codes the init-check _hash comparison (`const expectedHash = recomputeInitCheckHash(storyId, store, projectRoot); if (initCheck._hash !== expectedHash)`) instead of routing through the CHK-003 single trust predicate (initCheckHashMatches / initCheckSignatureIsValid) declared once in core/init-check-gate.ts precisely so no consumer re-invents this comparison. Two concrete consequences: (1) it performs a second independent store.readInitCheck read inside recomputeInitCheckHash rather than verifying the snapshot the caller already holds in `initCheck` -- the exact double-read/race pattern CHK-003 explicitly closed in machine.ts (module comment: verify against the SNAPSHOT already read, not a second read of the file). (2) initCheckHashMatches trims stored/expected hash strings and treats blank as untrusted, while the raw `!==` here does not, so a persisted _hash with incidental whitespace would be judged VALID by the real gate (canEnterInitCheckGuard / getGuardFailureReason, both correctly migrated to initCheckSignatureIsValid by this story) but reported [STALE] by this preflight row -- a live disagreement between the authoritative gate and its own preflight surveyor. Confirmed this is not caught by any existing test: init-preflight-smoke.ts assertAgreement() only asserts the aggregate report.gate.ready/blockedBy (which IS computed correctly via getGuardFailureReason at init-preflight.ts:287), never the individual init-check row status this function returns. Not touched by this diff, but directly falsifies the story-wide claim (repeated in init-check-gate.ts module doc and CLAUDE.md) that the trust predicate is declared once so it cannot silently diverge from what the gate uses -- this is exactly the remaining comparison site the story asked reviewers to rule out.
findings.dismissReason: Real defect, deferred with a tracked follow-up, not dropped. packages/main/src/handlers/init-preflight.ts is outside this story's scope contract and scope_contract_check runs in enforce mode: an earlier item in this same story edited that file, was refused, and correctly reverted. Fixing it here would require a contract extension mid-REVIEW. The follow-up carries the full diagnosis (open-coded comparison, second independent read reintroducing the race CHK-003 closed, missing trim/blank handling that makes preflight disagree with the real gate on a whitespace-bearing hash) plus the observation that init-preflight-smoke only asserts the aggregate gate.ready, never the row status, so the divergence is invisible to the suite. It also carries the sibling stale-enumeration at line 143. Recommend a repro-first RED pinning a whitespace hash before any fix.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:645 (selectorMatched = run.output.includes(pinSelector), exact substring) means CHK-002:happy:0's pinned selector "GREEN: both verdict fields are inside the signature domain." (checklist.json, recorded 2026-08-01T15:18 against red-b8df9-init-check-verdict-signature.mjs) is now permanently unmatchable: CHK-003 legitimately extended the SAME artifact's final conclusion print (tests/red/red-b8df9-init-check-verdict-signature.mjs:665-671) to "GREEN: both verdict fields are inside the signature domain, and the carry-forward refuses to re-sign..." (comma, not period, after domain). Reconfirmed live by re-running node bin/lattice.js validate --focus=b8df9-init-check-signature just now: the exact pinned string does not appear in current output. Because VerificationIntentPin is immutable once set (core/types.ts:287-291) and this artifact is a PERMANENT lattice.config.json validate.commands regression check (the CHK-002 waiver was withdrawn), this must-priority happy-path evidence can never again be re-earned as literally recorded. verification_evidence_refresh_stale (handlers/checklist.ts:1833-1877) re-executes the pinned command on staleness; on selector mismatch it falls to the demote path (checklist.ts:906-926), silently converting a mechanical:true receipt into mechanical:false with an auto-generated "receipt invalidated" reason while leaving result:pass untouched. Not currently blocking REVIEW->TEST (recorded receipt is intact), but materialHash has moved since this evidence was recorded (init-check-gate.ts/store.ts/handlers/init-check.ts/command-policy.ts all changed afterward via CHK-003/005/006), so the next legitimate refresh -- e.g. done_prepare --refreshStale, which CLAUDE.md requires before DONE -- will trigger the demotion. This is exactly the class of durability defect the review task flagged (a selector anchored to a mutable summary sentence rather than a stable per-row claim id), the same class that produced a finding against predecessor story B-49d4.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed by execution, then waived at the pin level with the reasoning recorded. Ran grep -F of the pinned selector against live artifact output: it fails, because CHK-003 legitimately extended the final conclusion line from '...signature domain.' to '...signature domain, and the carry-forward...'. The pin is immutable on first selector-bearing write, so it cannot be re-pinned and the evidence cannot be re-earned as recorded - the finding is correct on every point. Mitigation rather than a fix: the PROPERTY remains mechanically proven independently of the pin, because red-b8df9-init-check-verdict-signature.mjs is registered NON-OPTIONAL and reports 0 RED across 24 rows on every validate, with rows B1/B2/B3 covering exactly this intent. A permanent waiver now carries that distinction so the demotion at done_prepare --refreshStale is not mistaken for lost coverage. Also recorded the generalised lesson: my instruction to implementers ('marker names, never literal counts') was necessary but insufficient - this selector obeyed it and still broke. The correct rule is that a selector must be pinned to something no LATER work will legitimately reword: a stable row identifier or machine token, never a prose conclusion sentence.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts:391 (finding_add), :411 (scope_check_save), :412 (scope_question_resolve) still justify their reviewerWrite owner-lease exemption with "...bound by its REVIEW-phase reviewer-run/signature gate" / "...bound by its PLAN signature gate" / "...bound by its PLAN gate" -- the SAME unsupported inference (a content checksum is treated as if it binds WHO wrote the file, when INIT_CHECK_SALT/signInitCheck are exported source so anyone who can write the file can re-sign it) that this story just falsified for init_check_set (command-policy.ts:406) and that CHK-006's own verificationEvidence note (.lattice/story/actives/B-8df9/checklist.json, CHK-006:adversarial:0) explicitly names: "the sibling reviewerWrite reasons ... carry the same structural inference ... reported to the main agent unedited rather than reworded on unmeasured claims." The implementer was right not to silently rewrite these three (outside CHK-006 scope, and the story's own flag-do-not-polish rule), but the discovery was reported ONLY in evidence note prose and was never registered via finding_add -- findings.json before this review round held only F-001 (an unrelated CHK-002 userSees issue), so this specific discovery had no gate-visible, trackable artifact and was at real risk of being lost once the story reaches DONE. Filing it here so it becomes a scheduled, resolvable item rather than a claim buried in a verificationEvidence note.
findings.resolvedReason: Each of the three reasons was re-derived from its own signing function and handler, not reworded to match init_check_set. finding_add (:391): restated as deposit-only — the handler pushes one record under the story finding lock and never edits/removes an existing one, a pass-only record is normalized into an appended review-pass, no phase change, and every gate that spends a finding (story_advance, finding_resolve/finding_dismiss) is owner-gated; signFinding binds only storyId/id/desc/severity/timestamp/reviewRound/reviewRunId (+optional read-evidence/gapLog), does not even contain the agent field, and is exported source — so the signature clause was removed as a justification. scope_check_save (:411): the deposit-only argument is NOT available and I said so — store.writeScopeCheck replaces scope-check.json wholesale, dropping the previous verdict and any openQuestions resolutions; what is true is PLAN-only, no phase change, owner-gated consumer (story_review then story_advance) which also refuses a non-current reviewRound; signScopeCheck binds storyId/timestamp/reviewRound (+v2 features/summary/readManifest) with SCOPE_CHECK_SALT and signScopeCheck exported, and openQuestions outside the domain. scope_question_resolve (:412): premise is FALSE and is now flagged in the reason rather than reworded — handlers/scope-question-resolve.ts and the story-review.ts blocker message both say this is the main agent (owner) answering the reviewer question by anti-self-pardon design, the resolution field is deliberately outside the signature domain, the handler re-signs nothing and verifies no caller identity, and the PLAN gate only re-checks trim length >= 20; so a reviewerWrite-classified, lease-EXEMPT command directly clears a PLAN blocker on someone else story. ownershipClass values were NOT changed (that changes gate behaviour and needs its own story). Class-level doc comment (:40-43) rewritten the same way: the exemption is not bought by signatures, each entry must state what its write can do. Verified: npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/main clean, scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs verified, .lattice/story/actives/B-8df9/chk006-exemption-claims.mjs 0 FAILED / 10 claims, node bin/lattice.js validate all green (exit 0) with both red artifacts 0 RED / 24 rows and 0 FAILED / 17 rows. NOT covered: review_run_start (:198) and review_pass_set (:199) carry the same sentence shape and were left untouched per dispatch scope. Commit e65e3cbef0.

findings.desc: CHK-003:adversarial:0 (.lattice/story/actives/B-8df9/checklist.json) frozen desc claims "A file whose _hash was recomputed by an attacker over tampered content is still refused" -- execution REFUTES this (row H1 of tests/red/red-b8df9-init-check-verdict-signature.mjs:528-557, reconfirmed live just now: refusedBeforeReSigning=true verifiesAfterReSigning=true gateAdvancesOnTheReSignedRecord=true). INIT_CHECK_SALT is a public source constant, so an editor who re-signs with the product's own signInitCheck IS accepted. The implementer correctly recorded verdict=audit_only rather than a clean pass and, since checklist metadata is frozen from DEV, explicitly deferred "whether to re-word the intent or waive it" to the main agent. That deferred question IS substantively answered in docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md:121-124 ("Scope of the property this buys ... An editor who also re-signs is accepted ... never reviewer trustworthiness"), which names row H1 directly -- so I judge audit_only the honest disposition here, not a gap dressed as satisfaction; no reword/waiver is substantively required. The one loose end: CHK-002's analogous frozen-metadata conflict was closed with a discoverable finding (B-8df9:F-001, described in its own text as "the sanctioned channel for recording" a superseded pinned criterion), but CHK-003:adversarial:0 has no equivalent finding, so a reader of findings.json alone (without cross-referencing the decision doc or the evidence note) would not learn the adversarial intent is, as literally worded, false. Filing this low/non-blocking finding purely for audit-trail symmetry with F-001; recommend resolving by referencing story-lifecycle.md:121-124 rather than reopening PLAN.
findings.dismissReason: The filer itself judged audit_only the honest disposition and filed this only as a symmetry gap against the F-001 precedent. CHK-003's adversarial intent is empirically false - a re-signed tampered file IS accepted, because the salt is a public source constant - and the implementer recorded verdict=audit_only rather than a false pass, made the fact durable as artifact row H1, and the substantive question is resolved in docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md:121-124. The intent text is frozen from DEV by design and the honest disposition is already recorded. Rewording it would change nothing about what is true or what is proven.

findings.desc: quality-durability: .lattice/story/actives/B-8df9/checklist.json CHK-005:happy:0 and CHK-005:adversarial:0 (re-pinned via verification_evidence_add during this post-merge re-attestation) cite the markers GATED_INIT_STORY_ID=B-dcf9 and SIGNATURE_VERIFIES_UNDER_CURRENT_DOMAIN=false, both emitted only while B-dcf9 (an unrelated, currently-active, high-priority story) remains in phase INIT. These are docs-type attestations (mechanical:false, no CLI-enforced selector pin, per packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:682-689), so nothing gates on them today, but the evidence note explicitly claims the row is now durable/re-verifiable. As soon as B-dcf9 advances out of INIT (or a different story becomes the sole gated one), chk005-corpus-derivation.mjs will stop emitting that exact GATED_INIT_STORY_ID=B-dcf9 line, breaking the marker this row cites. This is precisely the failure class CHK-002:happy:0 waiver already documents for this same story (a selector must be pinned to something no later work/state change will legitimately alter, not a transient live value) — here the fragile value is a third-party stable-in-name-only system state rather than a prose conclusion line, but the durability failure mode is the same. Recommend re-pinning to a stable identifier (e.g. the corpus script line/row-id plus story-count semantics, or an explicit note that the row is a point-in-time snapshot rather than a live-reverifiable claim) rather than a live third-party phase-dependent value.
findings.resolvedReason: Correct, accepted in full, and the root cause is mine. Three lanes caught the same defect from three angles: quality saw the CHK-005 selectors pinned to which story happens to sit in INIT (B-dcf9 today); concept saw the CHK-006 selectors pinned to prose that command-policy.ts's own comment invites future editors to reword; test-coverage proved the decisive fact — docs-type intents route to the attestation-only branch of enforceAndStampEvidence BEFORE any caller-supplied selector is read, so NO selector, pin or receipt was ever persisted and mechanical stayed false. My note claiming the rows were "re-pinned with a stable selector, now mechanically re-verifiable" was therefore false from the moment it was written. It flipped no gate, but it put a false claim about evidence strength into a permanent audit trail — on the one story whose entire subject is that a signature must cover what its gate decides on, or the record will confidently mislead. Fix: appended a retraction to each of the four rows that withdraws the claim, states what they actually are (point-in-time attestations executed by hand on the merged tree), and records why they are not durably re-verifiable. Also recorded that the original author's decision to leave them unpinned was the better judgement. No selector remains claimed anywhere.

findings.desc: concept-drift: .lattice/story/actives/B-8df9/checklist.json CHK-004's three verificationEvidence waiver rows (happy/edge/adversarial) assert 'THIS WAIVER IS A FRAMEWORK GAP, NOT A DISPOSITION ... A user-approved withdrawal has no mechanical completion path, so this waiver is prose standing where proof should be. Filed as a framework defect; do not read it as evidence.' That specific claim was falsified by this same merge: B-45a5 ('Wire the existing item-level withdrawal helper into the two REVIEW-path gates', pulled in at merge commit ab5f930d9e) wires withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom(decision) into checkDispatchEvidence (packages/main/src/handlers/validate-channel.ts:305) AND into evaluateReviewCompleteness via withdrawnItemIntentRefs (packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:1672-1682, consumed at :2165-2167) -- exactly the mechanical completion path the waiver says does not exist, and it addresses precisely the concern the waiver raised ('whole-binding withdrawal would have dropped delivered CHK-003 coverage' -- the new mechanism withdraws by item id, not by whole acceptance binding). Recommend a corrective annotation (e.g. a review-pass note or a superseding evidence/audit entry pointing at B-45a5's fix) rather than leaving the claim unqualified in the durable record.
findings.resolvedReason: Correct. The three CHK-004 waiver notes assert a framework gap that story B-45a5 closed on 2026-08-19, and evidence being append-only meant nothing in the record said so. Appended a superseding annotation on CHK-004 recording that the gap is closed, naming the two wirings that closed it (withdrawnItemIntentRefs in core/proofstory.ts and the withdrawn bucket in checkDispatchEvidence), and citing the live verification: validate --channel prints withdrawn (SD-7319de10) on its own line outside the Covered list, and proofstory_review_completeness_check reports Gaps 0 with CHK-004's refs excluded from the required set. Recommend re-pinning both rows to a stable structural marker (e.g. extend chk006-exemption-claims.mjs to also assert a dedicated marker for 'the exemption reason states the signature limit' / 'the exemption is flagged by story id', or add a named constant in command-policy.ts that the grep can target instead of free prose) rather than grepping command-policy.ts's reason prose directly.

findings.desc: CHK-005:happy:0, CHK-005:adversarial:0, CHK-006:happy:0, CHK-006:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence notes claim a mechanical upgrade that did not occur: each note says (e.g.) "Re-pinned with a stable selector so this row is now mechanically re-verifiable rather than a bare command record." But these four intents are type=docs. enforceAndStampEvidence (packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:680-688) checks isExecutableIntentType (packages/main/src/core/verification.ts:98-102, EXECUTABLE_INTENT_TYPES={logic,cli,browser}) BEFORE consulting any caller selector; for a docs/manual intent it returns evidencePatch={mechanical:false, command, result} and never reads input.selector, never writes intent.verification={command,selector}. Confirmed on-disk in .lattice/story/actives/B-8df9/checklist.json: none of the four evidence rows carry a selector, a verification pin on the intent, or a receipt; mechanical stays false on all four -- byte-identical in shape to an ordinary unpinned bare-command attestation. No selector was actually persisted despite the note text. This does not currently flip any gate (coverageStatusForCoveredEvidence treats non-executable intent types as unconditionally covered regardless of mechanical, so these rows were covered before and after identically), but it is a false claim of stronger evidence written permanently into the append-only audit trail of a story whose entire subject is exactly this failure mode (see SD-7319de10: a mechanism that claims to prove something stronger than it does). Recommend appending a corrective docs_check row (evidence is append-only) on each of the four intentRefs whose note accurately says these are re-attested non-mechanical docs_check narrative judgments (type=docs intents cannot be selector-pinned by design), not selector-pinned mechanical rows.

It flipped no gate, but it put a false claim about evidence strength into a permanent audit trail — on the one story whose entire subject is that a signature must cover what its gate decides on, or the record will confidently mislead. Fix: appended a retraction to each of the four rows that withdraws the claim, states what they actually are (point-in-time attestations executed by hand on the merged tree), and records why they are not durably re-verifiable. Also recorded that the original author's decision to leave them unpinned was the better judgement. No selector remains claimed anywhere.

findings.desc: summary.json:6 actualTranscript overclaims evidence-strength: it says the behavior lane AND the delivery reviewer each built their own fixture and confirmed all three attacks (injection/erasure/rename). On record, only lattice-review-behavior RR-020 (RP-015) built a fixture testing all three attacks; the delivery reviewer transcript (delivery-check.json CHK-002 row) built its own fixture testing only ONE attack (hand-injected reviewer record / injection), not erasure or rename. Also unclear where four probes come from: only two out-of-suite fixtures are on record (behavior RR-020 covering all 3 attacks; delivery covering 1). The underlying three-attack conclusion IS true and IS backed by evidence (behavior RR-020 plus the shipped D1/D2/D3 rows), but the sentence misattributes which reviewer independently confirmed which attacks and inflates the probe count -- the exact overclaim-about-evidence-strength failure mode this story is about (cf. F-009/F-011/F-012).
findings.resolvedReason: Correct, and it is the third instance of this exact failure mode from me on this story. Verified the record rather than paraphrasing again: the behavior lane's fixture (RR-020/RP-015) covered three attacks - fabricated reviewer entry, erased critical issue, renamed agentId; the delivery reviewer's own fixture covered unsigned tampering plus the out-of-tool re-sign acceptance, not all three. My draft said "four independent probes" and implied both had confirmed all three. The conclusion was sound; the count and attribution were inflated. Fixed: actualTranscript now states precisely what each probe covered, names the re-sign case as the deliberate honest bound rather than a gap, and cites the shipped guard's H1 control row which asserts both halves mechanically (refusedBeforeReSigning=true, verifiesAfterReSigning=true). Also added pitfalls item (5) recording that this happened in the same round where I had explicitly warned your lane to watch for it - writing the warning is not protection against committing the error.
